question: Why does the blastocyst keep its membrane as it rolls through the uterus?
answer: The blastocyst keeps its membrane as a shield. It protects the cluster of cells while the cluster rolls along the uterine cavity. The membrane only breaks open where the uterus offers the right conditions.
move: The membrane stays shut until the right spot, then it opens.

web.label: A transparent bubble of cells rolls along a uterine cavity while the reader picks one of three reasons why its membrane is kept. The bubble opens only when it reaches a green OK zone.
